request: git_commit_guard is blind on a repository's first commit: currentBranch() shells `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which exits 128 on an unborn branch, so branchPolicy() reports notGit and skips the detached, topology, and consent checks. The identical body in .claude/hooks/lib/common.mjs:900 degrades branch_guard the same way. Resolve the branch via `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`, single-source it in lib/common.mjs, decide the fail-safe for an in-work-tree repo whose branch stays unresolvable, and amend docs/init/seed.md §18.4 + src/seed.template.md.
novelty_evidence: Corrects the shipped branch-aware-git-policy contract: docs/archive/2026-05-15/branch-aware-git-policy/spec.md:590 has a failure-mode row for detached HEAD (AC-005) and no row for an unborn branch, and scout.md:86 of the same workflow asserts the unborn case 'behaves the same as a normal branch. Fine.' Reproduced at d23c06b: the same scratch repo with protected_branches ['main'] returns allow before the first commit and deny after it.
track_reason: tdd-quickfix is the leaner candidate and covers the code defect, but the fix changes a consent-boundary contract that docs/init/seed.md §18.4 and src/seed.template.md state verbatim, so it carries a genesis amendment (CLAUDE.md Art. I.4). .claude/hooks/** is also in project.json security.sensitive_globs, so the security phase applies. spec-entry is the leanest track whose guardrails cover both.
